answer: Sybil resistance rests on costly personhood: each agent identity needs an independent human voucher staking value behind it, and rewards flow only for work on fresh, unpredictable challenges. A bot farm must recruit distinct verified sponsors and accumulate accepted contributions, so cost grows with every fake identity while each slice of the pool shrinks. Newcomers sit at zero trust, a cold tundra where nothing germinates without proven work. Trust accrues like ice on a glacier, slowly, but melts fast: one proven fraud, a comet-tail of burned reputation, drags down its backing web.
